threads_text: You can now text ChatGPT's Dot agent over iMessage or RCS, and it can text you first when there's news on a task you gave it. It's US Pro users only for now. Would you let an AI agent text you on its own?
caption:
OpenAI now lets you text Dot, its ChatGPT personal agent, over iMessage or RCS.
Send it texts, photos or voice memos with a task, and it texts you back with updates on its own.
The preview is for ChatGPT Pro users in the US.

Would you let an AI agent text you first?

site_article.headline: OpenAI lets ChatGPT Pro users in the US text their Dot agent over iMessage and RCS
site_article.dek: Dot can now take tasks by text, photo or voice memo and message users with updates on its own, starting with a US preview for Pro subscribers.
site_article.summary: OpenAI began letting users text Dot, its ChatGPT personal agent, through iMessage and RCS on October 28, 2026. The preview is available to ChatGPT Pro subscribers in the United States.
site_article.seo_title: ChatGPT's Dot agent now works over iMessage and RCS
site_article.seo_description: OpenAI now lets US ChatGPT Pro users text their Dot agent over iMessage or RCS, and Dot can text back with updates on tasks.
site_article.answer_summary: Yes, if you are a ChatGPT Pro subscriber in the United States. Open your Dot's profile in ChatGPT, select Texting and verify your phone number, according to Digital Trends.
site_article.hero_alt: OpenAI promotional graphic for its Dot agents.

paragraphs.text: OpenAI on October 28, 2026 began letting users text Dot, the personal agent it introduced in ChatGPT in late September, through Apple's iMessage and the RCS messaging standard on Android phones, according to Engadget and 9to5Mac.

Until now, Dot could only be reached inside ChatGPT on mobile, desktop and the web, 9to5Mac reported. OpenAI announced the change in posts from its ChatGPT account, saying that users could now text their Dot by popular request.

Users can send Dot text messages, photos and voice memos, for example to hand it a task or ask it to keep an eye on something. Dot can then message the user on its own with relevant updates, Engadget reported. Digital Trends said Dot can also send an approval link so a user can review a request inside the app.

According to Digital Trends, Dot can use a user's ChatGPT conversations and connected channels to decide where to send an update, and users can limit texts to urgent matters while routine updates stay in ChatGPT. Information that Dot saves to its memory is shared between ChatGPT and text, so context carries over, Engadget reported.

The feature is rolling out as a preview to ChatGPT Pro subscribers in the United States, Engadget and Digital Trends reported, and Digital Trends described it as a beta. Engadget noted that Dots are not available on the Plus plan.

To set it up, users open their Dot's profile in ChatGPT and select Texting. Digital Trends said users then verify a phone number, save the contact Dot sends back and message it. iPhone owners need iMessage turned on and Android owners need RCS enabled. Conversations are one to one only, with no group chats, phone calls or FaceTime, although calling Dot inside ChatGPT still works.

OpenAI said it worked with the company Linq to provide messaging support and carried out extensive penetration testing, according to Engadget. The company says only the user can text their Dot and that Dot can only text that user. Both 9to5Mac and Digital Trends reported that setup does not give Dot or OpenAI access to a user's other text conversations.

The launch comes a week after Anthropic introduced Claude Duet, its own personal agent. Engadget reported that Claude Duet currently requires joining a US waitlist and that Anthropic plans to offer it to subscribers of its $20 a month Pro plan.

In NeuraFeed's reading, moving Dot into the default messaging app is an attempt to make an AI agent feel like a contact rather than a website. An agent that can start the conversation is also a bigger privacy and trust question than a chatbot that only answers, which is why OpenAI put its security limits up front. For now the audience is small, since the preview is limited to the most expensive consumer plan in one country.

The next thing to watch is whether OpenAI extends Dot and its texting feature to Plus subscribers or to users outside the United States, and how quickly Anthropic opens Claude Duet beyond its waitlist.
